items.title: What industrial drone deployments reveal about real-world autonomy challenges
items.summary: Supervised autonomous UAV inspection at an industrial facility. | Source: ZenaDrone An autonomous drone can complete a carefully planned inspection route in a controlled environment and still struggle with the same route at an operating industrial facility. A steel structure may obstruct satellite signals, reflective equipment may distort depth measurements, and a wind gust may push the aircraft outside its planned trajectory. Each disturbance can be manageable in isolation. The difficulty emerges when several occur simultaneously. This exposes a fundamental challenge in industrial drone autonomy: performance depends on interactions between subsystems whose assumptions are rarely independent. items.title: From Commercial Scale to Embodied Intelligence: The Next Challenge for Robotics
items.summary: Robotics is advancing rapidly. New AI models and increasingly capable hardware are expanding what machines can perceive, understand and do, bringing more adaptable and general-purpose robots closer to practical use. But greater capability does not automatically translate into commercial readiness. In supermarkets, hotels, airports and other working environments, robots must navigate changing conditions, operate alongside people, integrate with existing workflows and perform reliably over time. The challenge is not simply what a robot can do, but whether it can do it consistently and at scale.
